title: Memory slab fragmentation and FlashAttention behavior
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This scratchpad collects notes and early experiments around an operationally-observed slow tail behavior and occasional OOMs that correlate with FlashAttention runs after periods of mixed-length traffic. Hypothesis: allocator fragmentation (GPU slab/pool) combined with FlashAttention and some fused-op kernels is causing transient large allocations or suboptimal kernel paths, which increases latency p95/p99 and sometimes triggers OOMs on node-level capacity that previously handled the same throughput.

Why I care (symptoms):
- p50 unchanged, but p95/p99 for token-step latency spikes after a busy period with varied sequence-length requests.
- repro: runs for ~30–60 minutes with seq mix [16, 64, 512] then sudden spike in 95th from ~7ms to ~45ms for subsequent 512 tokens.
- in some runs, cudaMalloc failures or fallback to slower kernel paths reported in logs (see linked SERV-5212).

Key background/context notes:
- We use a custom GPU memory pool (slab allocator) that keeps free slabs for reuse.
- FlashAttention prefers contiguous workspaces sized by B*L*K factors; paged-attention variants allocate smaller windows but more frequently.
- Fused ops (fused qkv + rms_norm + dropout fusions) sometimes choose alternative kernels when workspace shapes mismatch.
- Mixed sequence-length traffic increases fragmentation risk because lots of different workspace sizes are created and freed.

Experiments run so far (commands and brief results):

Experiment 1 — baseline replicant (no extra pooling changes)
- workload: synthetic rps=120, seq mix 16:40%, 64:40%, 512:20% over 45m
- profiler: nvprof + custom tracing (timestamped allocations)
- result: steady p50=6.4ms, p95 period 6–9ms until 27m, then p95 jumps to 42–56ms; logs show some cudaMalloc timed out (non-fatal) and kernel fallback to slower FlashAttn variant.

Experiment 2 — aggressive slab merging (keep only two slab sizes: small(64MB) and large(1GB))
- change: runtime config "gpu.slab.compact_levels=2"
- result: fewer unique slab sizes, p95 increased slightly in warmup but remained stable over time (p95 10–14ms), no cudaMalloc failures during 1h run.
- notes: memory usage up ~6% due to rounding to large slabs.

Experiment 3 — disable fused ops for qkv (force unfused kernels)
- change: env FORCE_UNFUSED_QKV=1
- result: average kernel time up ~8%, but p95 tail behavior improved: spikes reduced and no OOMs observed.

Experiment 4 — FlashAttention workspace pre-reserve for largest model shapes
- change: prewarm alloc: allocate workspace for B=16,L=1024,K=64 on start and hold
- result: p95 stable but memory overhead large; helpful in preventing cudaMalloc latency during first heavy request.

Micro-profiling notes (what traces showed):
- Allocation timeline: many frees happen in size ranges that are not coalesced by our pool; free list contains small fragments that together exceed needed large workspace but allocator cannot merge across slab boundaries.
- Kernel chooser logs: when an allocation takes >5ms, kernel path sometimes switches to fallback (safe but slower) path.
- Some fused kernels probe for available workspace and then do a cudaMalloc if pool cannot satisfy exact size (this triggers new slab creation and increases fragmentation).

Hypotheses we want to test next (ranked):
1) Slab-level compaction — if we periodically compact or proactively reserve large slabs during low load windows, fragmentation spikes will disappear.
2) Adaptive workspace rounding — round requested workspace sizes up to nearest class to reduce variety and increase reuse (tradeoff: some extra memory).
3) Kernel handshake change — modify fused kernel to accept a split-workspace (two contiguous allocations) to avoid large single allocation requirement.
4) Pager-friendly allocation — for paged attention, change page size to align with slab sizes to improve reuse.

Quick proposed experiments (short actionable):
- A: runtime toggle: gpu.slab.compact_interval = 5m (compact every 5 minutes) + run standard replicate load for 2h; measure p95/p99 and count of new slab allocations per minute.
- B: introduce rounding policy: workspace.round_to = [64KB, 1MB, 16MB] (tune thresholds); run 45m mixing trial and measure overall memory overhead vs p95 improvements.
- C: patch fused-op kernel to query pool for two blocks and record whether it used one or two; run with heavy 512 seq load to check fallback frequency.

Operational mitigations we can roll quickly:
- If p95 spike observed, automatically trigger a short warmup job that pre-allocates a few large workspaces for all hottest models (cheap to implement via existing admin API).
- Expose "workspace rounding" knob in per-model config for customers to opt in when running mixed-length traffic.
- Add instrumented counters: allocations_by_size_class, slab_merges_attempted, allocation_latency_ms histogram to Console for easier debugging.

Open questions and unknowns:
- What exact allocator implementation detail causes inability to merge adjacent free segments across slab boundaries? Is it our use of fixed-size slabs or CUDA's allocation granularity? Need SRE + infra allocator deep-dive.
- Does FlashAttention's internal memory pattern (temporary K/V buffers) cause short-lived bursts that are not well served by our pool?
- Are there any hardware-specific behaviors (A100 vs H100) for allocation latency that bias toward fragmentation? Quick HW matrix needs to be run.

Notes on metrics to capture (for future runs):
- per-node: num_slab_sizes, active_free_fragments_count, total_free_bytes, largest_free_contiguous
- per-request: alloc_attempt_count, alloc_latency_ms, which_kernel_variant_used, fallback_flag
- per-model: reserved_workspace_bytes, rounding_policy_applied (yes/no)

Example log snippets (sanitized):
[2024-10-03T14:17:22Z] alloc_request(size=27852800) -> pool_miss -> cudaMalloc(27.8MB) took 6.2ms -> used flashattn_safe_kernel
[2024-10-03T14:17:23Z] free(27.8MB) -> freed_into_slab(64MB) -> leftover_fragment=36MB
[2024-10-03T14:48:07Z] alloc_request(size=980000000) -> pool_miss -> cudaMalloc(980MB) failed -> OOM -> fallback to smaller-kernel-path or request rerouted

Next steps (owners and rough ETA):
- A: Run compaction interval experiment (owner: Rajat) — 3 days to implement + 2 days runs + 1 day analysis.
- B: Implement rounding policy (owner: Samir) — 5 days for runtime change + 2 days evaluation.
- C: Hardware matrix runs (owner: Elena) — schedule 1 week on H100 and A100 pools.
- D: Add allocation telemetry to Console (owner: Ava) — 4 days to add counters + dashboards.

Decision criteria for rollout:
- If compaction or rounding reduces p99 by >=30% with <10% extra memory overhead, consider defaulting rounding for hosted tier and enable compaction for Dedicated.

Loose notes and ideas not yet tested:
- Try jemalloc-style coalescing within pool; tradeoffs with lock contention.
- For paged-attention, maintain per-page-size freelists and prebind pages to models with heavy long-sequence traffic.
- Consider moving to a GPU virtual memory abstraction that avoids cudaMalloc/free churn by using a long-lived device allocation and implementing suballocator with mmap-like semantics (big engineering lift).

References and context links:
- See linked PR #1427 for added allocator metrics and initial instrumentation.
- SERV-5212: customer incident with repeated OOMs after mixed-length load spike.
- Experimental dashboards: internal link in Confluence (linked_artifacts above).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc lightweight — move final results into a /postmortems or playbook page once we have reproducible thresholds.

End of scratchpad.
